intro.title: Most people who come to us are holding one end of a story: a city a grandparent left, a refusal from the Interior Ministry, a surname that changed at a border.
intro.p1: Our work is to turn that into a file an authority will accept. Decker Pex Levi practises immigration, visa and citizenship law and nothing else, from Tel Aviv and Jerusalem, in eight languages.
intro.p2: We take on matters with a reasonable prospect of success, say so candidly when there is none, and carry the ones we accept to the end, including appeals.

law.title: In 2020 the citizenship laws changed. Most families never heard.
law.p1: Germany and Austria widened the routes for descendants of people who lost citizenship through persecution. Descendants must prove the line to the German or Austrian ancestor, and that the ancestor was forced to give up that citizenship.
law.p2: We were among the first firms in Israel to file these cases. Six questions tell you which route your family history points to, then a free call with one of our lawyers tells you what the records will need.

stages.title: Six stages. One of them is yours.
stages.lede: You tell us the story and hand over whatever papers exist. Records, translations, filing and the authority are ours.
